The firm's archived news, 1999-2019, from the Common Crawl captures of
indexventures.com (sources/wayback/cc-manifest.json):
  2008-2013 PHP site   /news/index/news_id/<n>: one press release or cutting per
                       page (h2#news-title, h4#news-date, body); every news page
                       also lists dated titles in <ul id="results">.
  2013      /blog/index/...: the firm's blog posts.
  2014-2019 Drupal     /news-room/news|blog|index-insight/<slug>.
One row per item with its capture URL (the citation where the live site dropped
the page), date, title, kind, the sentences that name a round, and the base
companies its title names. Output sources/wayback/news-archive.json.
An announcement is class 1 for the round it NAMES; it asserts an entry only
where it says so in words (COLLECTION.md s6).

The acquisition will strengthen eBay’s global marketplace and payments platform, while opening several new lines of business and creating significant new monetization opportunities for the company.
Buyers will gain an easy way to talk to sellers quickly and get the information they need to buy, and sellers can more easily build relationships with customers and close sales.
The acquisition also enables eBay and Skype to pursue entirely new lines of business.

Transaction and Financial Information eBay will acquire all of the outstanding shares of privately-held Skype for a total up-front consideration of approximately €2.1 billion, or approximately $2.6 billion, which is comprised of $1.3 billion in cash and the value of 32.4 million shares of eBay stock, which are subject to certain restrictions on resale.
Shareholders representing approximately 40% of the Skype shares chose to receive a single payment in cash and eBay stock at the close of the transaction.

Shareholders representing the remaining 60% of the Skype shares chose to receive a reduced up-front payment in cash and eBay stock at the close plus potential future earn-out payments which are based on performance-based goals for active users, gross profit and revenue.
For Q4-05, eBay expects the acquisition to be dilutive to pro forma and GAAP earnings per share by $0.01 and $0.04 respectively.
